symptom: `alter settings` writes a microflow, entity or constant name that does not exist, reports success, and `mxcli check --references` calls the script valid — the build then fails with **CE1613** *"The selected microflow/constant no longer exists"*. A misspelled constant is worse than a dangling pointer: the override is **created** for a constant that does not exist, leaving dead configuration data
cause: Settings were the ONLY statement family that resolved nothing. `--references` walks `validateWithContext`, whose switch had no `*ast.AlterSettingsStmt` case at all, so the qualified names in `AfterStartupMicroflow` / `BeforeShutdownMicroflow` / `HealthCheckMicroflow`, workflow `UserEntity` and the constant override went straight to the writer
file: `mdl/executor/validate_settings_refs.go` (`validateSettingsReferences`, `validateSettingsConstantRef`), wired into `mdl/executor/validate.go` (the `AlterSettingsStmt` case + `scriptContext.constants`) and into `alterSettings` itself; index helper `buildConstantQualifiedNames` in `mdl/executor/helpers.go`
insight: Put the guard in the **handler**, and have check call the same functions — that is what makes `exec` refuse exactly what `check` reports, including under `--no-check`, and it is why the exec-time call passes a **nil script context**: by then the earlier statements have run, so anything the script created is really in the project. Three cases a naive resolver gets wrong, each with a test: an **empty value clears** the setting (Studio Pro's "(none)") and must not be resolved; a document **created earlier in the same script** is not missing (the escape hatch every other family has, which is why the fixture pair is a `.fail.mdl` AND a passing control); and **dropping** a constant override must stay legal even when the constant is gone, or there is no way to tidy up after deleting one. Note the two `ValidateProgram`s are different passes — the package-level one (which `exec` runs) has only a project PATH, while the reference pass has a connected backend, so a check needing project reads cannot live in the first. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/274-settings-reference-validation.mdl` + `274-settings-reference-valid.mdl` — a plain `.mdl`, NOT `.fail.mdl`: `make check-mdl` runs `mxcli check` without a project, and a rule that resolves names against the model cannot decide anything there, so the file checks clean and `.fail.mdl` would report "negative test unexpectedly passed" — a working rule made to look regressed. The Makefile documents this above `check-mdl` (#891/#892); CI caught it here. Issue #274
